findings.problem: The voice says to write four with base two because the other term is two to the power X, but never says why matching bases helps, so a student does not see where this is heading.
findings.fix: Add one short sentence: with base two, four to the power X turns into the square of two to the power X, so the equation becomes a quadratic.

findings.problem: On "The other term" the whole of −3(2^x)+2=0 lights up, so the student cannot tell which part is the two to the power X being named.
findings.fix: Split the question line so 2^x is its own token, and light only that token on "The other term".

findings.problem: Line 2 just appears, so the student does not see that 2^{2x} has taken the place of 4^x in the equation.
findings.fix: Move the 2^{2x} from line 1 down into the first slot of line 2 (from + move) as the voice says "two to the power two X".

findings.problem: The voice says "two X is the same as X times two", but nothing is written until the next beat.
findings.fix: Write 2x = x × 2, or the 2^{x×2} part of line 3, on those words in beat 7.

findings.problem: a² − 3a + 2 = 0 appears whole, so the student does not see which part of line 2 became a² and which became 3a.
findings.fix: As each part is said, move the a² from line 3 and the 3a from line 5 into the new line.

findings.problem: "So X equals zero" jumps straight from two to the power zero without the reason, and this beat must make sense on its own when jumped to.
findings.fix: Say "Both sides have base two, so the powers are equal: X equals zero", and light the line as in beat 18.
